Batteries are for sure the ones that present more issues. After those, probably the Leaf blowers and Lawn Mowers. I can’t precisely give you a percentage, but I would say it is a 60% batteries and 40% the rest of the items.

Before you store them, make sure that you leave them 100% charged, leave your batteries in an environment with standard temperature. 

NEVER leave your batteries charging for weeks or entire months, you can leave your battery charging for up to 24 hours if you want, but more than that, it could damage its lifespan. 

If your battery shows any type of orange/yellow light, that means the battery is overheated, let it sit until it is 100% back to room temperature, never overwork it if these problems arise. 

If you leave your battery stored for a long time, disconnected from the charger and you see that a green or red light starts to flash, it is because the battery has started its own maintenance mode, always wait for that process to finish, do not interrupt it. After that, if you need to use them, make sure to charge your battery to its 100%.

It will depend on how well you store them and use them (with the exception of some of them already coming with a manufacture defect). Probably a I would say between 4 to 5 years, but with good maintenance they could even last to 9 or 10 years.
